01. Qualified Candidates must be either be currently registered with the California Board of Behavioral Sciences (BBS). Please select what you currently hold and attach a copy along with your application. Options: Associate Marriage and Family Therapist | Associate Clinical Social Worker | Associate Professional Clinical Counselor | I am not currently registered with the California Board of Behavioral Sciences

02. To be fully evaluated as a qualified candidate for this position, you must submit the supplemental questionnaire. Options: Yes, I will attach the required supplemental questionnaire found at https://tinyurl.com/ClinicianPVSD | No, I will not be attaching the supplemental questionnaire, and understand that my application will be considered incomplete.
Maintain District standards of excellent customer service and professional behavior in various and sometimes challenging situations.
Access and monitor District email daily to receive important updates from school and District administration.
Participate in staff development and in-service training programs as assigned.
Meet with students and families and compile social case histories.
Provide ongoing 1:1, group, or family counseling sessions.
Maintain regular contact with the parent/guardian to address the needs of the students (if applicable).
Research, develop, and implement evidence-based practices to support student social emotional development.
Utilize assessment data to make recommendations for interventions and strategies to support student engagement, attendance, behavior, and academic progress.
Interpret and explain factors pertaining to the needs of the students and families.
Refer students to appropriate agencies and coordinate with other agencies in support of students.
Provide outreach and support to students and families to successfully address chronic absenteeism.
Conduct and facilitate support groups, as necessary.
Consult with school staff regarding school-wide behavior supports.
Identify and provide intervention strategies for children, including case management and crisis intervention.
Coordinate parent education opportunities.
Coordinate, collaborate, and consult with Positive Behavior Intervention Team members.
Coordinate and support social work intern candidates in order to amplify services.
Attend related meetings and trainings as appropriate.
Provide relevant staff with trainings.
Conduct home visits providing strategies and intervention to families to support student and family needs.

Participate in intervention supports for students with identified attendance, behavioral and emotional challenges aligned to the school’s Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS) and Positive Behavioral Interventions and Supports (PBIS) framework.
Collaboratively work with parents, students, school counselors, school psychologists, teachers, school administrators, and other related service providers to support students’ identified needs.
Serve as member/consultant to the district and school site MTSS and PBIS teams.
